sn21.3:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.
sn21.3:1.3: Now on that occasion the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna were dwelling at Rājagaha in a single dwelling in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.
sn21.3:1.4: Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. He exchanged greetings with the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and,
sn21.3:1.5: when they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him:
sn21.3:2.1: "Friend Moggallāna, your faculties are serene, your facial complexion is pure and bright.
sn21.3:2.2: Has the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna spent the day in a peaceful dwelling?"
sn21.3:2.3: "I spent the day in a gross dwelling, friend,
sn21.3:2.4: but I did have some Dhamma talk."
sn21.3:2.5: "With whom did the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna have some Dhamma talk?"
sn21.3:2.6: "I had some Dhamma talk with the Blessed One, friend."
sn21.3:2.7: "But the Blessed One is far away, friend. He is now dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park.
sn21.3:2.8: Did the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna approach the Blessed One by means of spiritual power,
sn21.3:2.9: or did the Blessed One approach the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna by means of spiritual power?"
sn21.3:2.10: "I didn't approach the Blessed One by means of spiritual power, friend,
sn21.3:2.11: nor did the Blessed One approach me by means of spiritual power.
sn21.3:2.12: Rather, the Blessed One cleared his divine eye and divine ear element to communicate with me,
sn21.3:2.13: and I cleared my divine eye and divine ear element to communicate with the Blessed One."
sn21.3:2.14: "What kind of Dhamma talk did the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna have with the Blessed One?"
sn21.3:3.1: "Here, friend, I said to the Blessed One:
sn21.3:3.2: 'Venerable sir, it is said, "one with energy aroused, one with energy aroused."
sn21.3:3.3: In what way, venerable sir, does one have energy aroused?'
sn21.3:3.4: The Blessed One then said to me:
sn21.3:3.5: 'Here, Moggallāna, a bhikkhu with energy aroused dwells thus:
sn21.3:3.6: "Willingly, let only my skin, sinews, and bones remain, and let the flesh and blood dry up in my body, but I will not relax my energy so long as I have not attained what can be attained by manly strength, by manly energy, by manly exertion."
sn21.3:3.7: It is in such a way, Moggallāna, that one has aroused energy.'
sn21.3:3.8: Such, friend, is the Dhamma talk that I had with the Blessed One."
sn21.3:4.1: "Friend, compared to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna we are like a few grains of gravel
sn21.3:4.2: compared to the Himalayas, the king of mountains.
sn21.3:4.3: For the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna is of such great spiritual power and might that if so he wished he could live on for an aeon."
sn21.3:5.2: we are like a few grains of salt compared to a barrel of salt.
sn21.3:5.3: For the Venerable Sāriputta has been extolled, lauded, and praised in many ways by the Blessed One:
sn21.3:6.3: So a bhikkhu who has gone beyond
sn21.3:6.4: At best can only equal him.'"
sn21.3:7.1: In this manner both these great nāgas rejoiced in what was well stated and well declared by the other.
